## 🧠 Introduction

This project investigates how student background, academic programs, and institutional characteristics influence post-graduation earnings. We use two comprehensive datasets from the U.S. Department of Education’s College Scorecard:

- **Institution-Level Dataset**: Summarizes outcomes and demographics at the college level
- **Field-of-Study Dataset**: Provides earnings, debt, and aid data at the program level (major × institution × credential)

To build statistically sound and interpretable models, we must first address the **dimensionality** of these datasets. The institution dataset contains over 3,000 variables, and the field-of-study dataset has nearly 200. Many of these variables are irrelevant, redundant, poorly populated, or domain-specific.

---


## 🧰 Dataset Loading and Preparation

We load and clean the two datasets using `tidyverse` and `janitor`. We then apply each of the above criteria sequentially to create a reduced working dataset suitable for analysis and modeling.


```{r}
# Load institution-level dataset. Modify this to your local filepath. 
# Remembrer that the file can´t be in the repo due to the 100mb limitations. 

path_to_institutions <- "/Users/luisgarciamontero/Downloads/Most-Recent-Cohorts-Institution.csv"
path_to_field <- "/Users/luisgarciamontero/Downloads/Most-Recent-Cohorts-Field-of-Study.csv"


institution_data <- read_csv(path_to_institutions) %>%
  clean_names()

# Load field-of-study-level dataset
fieldofstudy_data <- read_csv(path_to_field) %>%
  clean_names()
```
```{r}
# Check dimensions and structure
dim(institution_data)
glimpse(institution_data)

# Skim summary (high-level EDA)
skim(institution_data)

```

```{r}
# Check dimensions and structure
dim(fieldofstudy_data)
glimpse(fieldofstudy_data)
# Skim summary (high-level EDA)
skim(fieldofstudy_data)
```
